# NOMANA-IT Documentation

> Documentation for the NOMANA-IT product suite — Liberty Framework, NomaUBL (French e-invoicing), Nomasx-1 / Nomajde (JD Edwards), and JDE API tools. Full text: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/llms-full.txt.

- [Liberty Core](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/getting-started/): Liberty Core — modular React framework with reusable UI components, context providers and application management tools for building modern apps.
- [Creating a New React App with Liberty Core](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/new-project/): Step-by-step guide to bootstrap a new React project with Liberty Core: OIDC authentication, translations and error handling included.
- [Applications Configuration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/applications/)
- [AppProvider Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/appprovider/)
- [Authentication & Token Management](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/authentication/)
- [ErrorBoundary Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/error-boundary/)
- [Modules Configuration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/modules/)
- [Theme Configuration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/themes/)
- [TranslationProvider Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/translations/)
- [useMediaQuery & useDeviceDetection](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/use-media-query/)
- [Users Configuration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/users/)
- [AI Assistant](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/ai-assistant/): The framework exposes an Anthropic tool-use assistant at /chat. Every SQL query and HTTP endpoint of every connector the caller can run becomes a tool the assistant can pick. Setup with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the tool-generation contract, per-role tool gating and conversation history.
- [Internationalization](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/apps/i18n/): How the framework picks the language for labels, dictionary entries and error messages — X-Liberty-Lang request header, per-user preference, falling back to the default. How to add a new language and override labels per app or per environment.
- [Apps](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/apps/overview/): A Liberty app groups connectors, screens, menus, dashboards, charts and jobs around one business domain. Apps are surfaced in the workspace selector at the top of the sidebar, edited per-entity from each Settings tab, and packaged as zip exports for transfer between environments.
- [Plugins](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/apps/plugins/): How to write custom Python code that the framework calls — Nomaflow job step callables, password validators, dispatch hooks. Drop a Python module under liberty-apps/plugins/, reference it by import path from TOML, the framework wires sys.path and calls it with the runtime context.
- [Build the tree](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/build-the-tree/): The tree editor — add folders and items, drag to reorder, indent/outdent to reparent, clone, rename, find usages. Every action's exact button and behaviour.
- [Item types](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/item-types/): The four leaf kinds — query / endpoint / dashboard / page — what each opens, the target field's shape, the connector rule, and when to reach for each.
- [Make a connector an app](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/make-connector-an-app/): A connector becomes an 'app' visible in the top switcher when it has a menu attached and show_in_switcher is on. Plus how the optional home field decides the landing page.
- [Menus — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/overview/): The Menus page, the flat-items-linked-by-parent model, the four leaf kinds (query / endpoint / dashboard / page), and how attaching a menu turns a connector into an app.
- [Permissions and roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/permissions-and-roles/): The roles filter on a menu item, the underlying sql / api permission inherited from the target, how empty folders collapse, and how the menu prunes per user.
- [Translations and icons](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/translations-and-icons/): Per-language label overrides with the `l` map (l.fr, l.de, …) and Lucide icon names on menu items. Conventions and fallbacks for both.
- [Packages](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/packages/): Ship configuration from one Liberty install to another. Settings → Package: pick a few screens / menu items / dashboards as seeds, the dependency walker pulls in everything they reach (queries, dictionary, charts), and the package exports as a ZIP. On the target install, upload + pick a merge strategy (merge / overwrite / replace all). Same UI handles both sides.
- [Deploy and debug](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/plugins/deploy-and-debug/): The apps repo layout, LIBERTY_APPS_DIR, the dev shell with uvicorn --reload, the production deploy pattern, log lines you'll grep for, and the testing setup.
- [ETL primitives](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/plugins/etl-primitives/): The liberty.etl toolkit — six async helpers your plugin callables compose into ETL flows: copy_query_to_table, snapshot_rows, delete_rows, truncate_table, insert_audit_record, run_query.
- [Plugins — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/plugins/overview/): A plugin is a Python package on disk that Liberty makes importable at startup. It carries custom callables your Nomaflow python steps reference — the escape hatch for anything declarative steps can't express.
- [Write a callable](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/plugins/write-a-callable/): The function contract for a python step's callable — signature, auto-injected kwargs (connectors / ctx / settings), return-value normalisation, sync vs async, error and cancellation semantics.
- [Clone a query or a connector](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/clone/): Duplicate one query inside a connector, duplicate every CRUD query of a table, or clone a whole application (connector + dictionary + screens + menu + dashboards + charts).
- [Create a custom query](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/create-custom/): Write a standalone query by hand — the Unclassified tab, the editor form, the writable gate, the params block, the SQL editor with autocompletion.
- [Create from a database table](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/create-from-database/): The CRUD Wizard — point Liberty at an existing table, tick the columns, get the four CRUD queries auto-generated and saved in one click.
- [Queries — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/overview/): How Liberty's Connectors page is organised — Tables / Unclassified / Sequences / Lookups — and the four kinds of queries each tab manages.
- [Parameter binding](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/parameter-binding/): How `:placeholder` params get values at runtime — declared defaults, screen-column sources, reserved built-ins like #LOGIN_USER# / #SYSDATE#, and per-call literal overrides.
- [Per-dialect SQL variants](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/per-dialect-sql/): Ship one Liberty query with different SQL on Postgres, Oracle, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite and DB2 — the per-dialect `sql` map, when to use it, common gotchas.
- [Sequences and lookups](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/sequences-and-lookups/): The Scaffold modal — tick a table and a column, get a generated sequence (next id) or lookup (value + label) query plus the matching dictionary entry, saved in one click.
- [Screen Creation Assistant](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screen-assistant/): A guided wizard that turns a set of database tables — or an existing connector query — into a working screen, dialog and menu item in one pass. Pick the source, choose the grid columns (default shared view), optionally lay dialog columns into tabs, review the dictionary, place a menu entry, create.
- [Actions and lifecycle](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/actions-and-lifecycle/): The Actions tab — toolbar buttons, row context menu, dialog hooks (on_load / on_save / on_cancel), row hooks (on_insert / on_update / on_delete), and the seven core action types.
- [Columns](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/columns/): The Columns tab — set each column's display title, format, dictionary reference, edit rule, default and filtering once; both the grid and the dialog use them.
- [Conditional fields](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/conditional-fields/): Make a dialog field appear, be required or be locked only when another field has a specific value — visible_when / required_when / disabled_when on ColumnHint and ScreenField.
- [Create a screen from a query](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/create-from-query/): Wire a `_get` query to a fresh screen — the General tab and the Queries tab walked through field by field; the grid appears, edits land via the write queries.
- [Dialog builder](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/dialog-builder/): The Visual Builder — a three-column Figma-style canvas (Palette / Canvas / Inspector) where you drag fields onto tabs, set properties, wire lookups and add per-tab actions.
- [Nested tabs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/nested-tabs/): Embed a child-record form (nested_form) or a related-rows grid (nested_table) in a dialog tab — same dialog, multiple data sources.
- [Screens — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/overview/): The Screens page — left scope bar of apps, flat list of screens, click to open the Screen Designer's 7 tabs (General / Queries / Columns / Dialog / Actions / Row menu / Export).
- [Encrypted secrets](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/encrypted-secrets/): The 🔒 toggle that encrypts secret fields at rest — what gets encrypted, how AES-256-GCM is wired, where the master key lives, the ENC: prefix, and the rotation story.
- [License key](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/license-key/): What the license gates (the bundled vendor products — Nomasx-1, Nomajde, NomaUBL …), where to set it (Settings → App is the canonical path; LIBERTY_LICENSE_KEY env var still works as a fallback), and what happens when it's missing or expired.
- [Secure — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/overview/): Who can sign in (local or OIDC), what they can do (roles + permissions with allow/deny grammar), and what's encrypted at rest. The two layers of Liberty's security model.
- [Roles and permissions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/roles-and-permissions/): Compose roles with the PermissionPicker — baseline (No access / Full access) plus allow / deny rules per surface. The full grammar, the resolution order, the standard recipes.
- [Sign-in — local and OIDC](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/sign-in/): Pick the identity backend (TOML or DB), configure local users, optionally enable OIDC against any compliant provider (Keycloak, Azure AD, Auth0, Okta…). What the user sees at sign-in.
- [Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/users/): The Settings → Access → Users tab — add local users, manage OIDC users that landed at first sign-in, assign roles, toggle is_active and is_superuser, reset passwords.
- [App settings](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/settings-app/): Settings → App is the master editor for app.toml — four collapsible sections (App, License, AI Assistant, OpenID Connect) covering host/port, the license key, the AI assistant configuration and OIDC SSO. Sensitive fields (license.key, ai.api_key, oidc.client_secret) round-trip masked and are encrypted at rest with the install master key. Most changes take effect live — only host / port / log_level need a server restart.
- [Charts](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/charts/): A chart wraps a connector query into a Recharts-rendered visualisation. Defined in Settings → Charts, picked from the builder by type (line, bar, column, pie, donut, area, scatter), with the axis fields, series, colours, legend and refresh interval set in the same form.
- [Framework settings](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/app-toml/): Every framework-wide setting — app name, default database pool, authentication backend, OIDC, AI provider, master encryption key, license — edited from Settings → Framework. The builder is schema-driven; this page lists every field, what it does and where it shows up.
- [Config history & versioning](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/config-history/): Every config save is snapshotted, every screen save captures its dependency closure as a restorable bundle, version changes are logged, and the bundled release notes are readable in-app — all under Settings → History.
- [Encryption & secrets](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/encryption-secrets/): Connector passwords, API tokens and OIDC secrets are stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Every secret field in the Settings UI has a 🔒 toggle to switch between plain and encrypted; the master key sits in the environment, never on disk. Rotation is online via legacy keys.
- [Environment variables](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/environment-variables/): Every LIBERTY_* environment variable documented — database URL, JWT signing key, master encryption key, license key, AI key, apps directory, OIDC settings — with the file it overrides and the default applied when unset.
- [Hot-reload](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/hot-reload/): Every per-section TOML edit done in the Settings UI or pushed via POST /admin/reload is applied to the running framework without a restart. This page documents what reloads, what stays in flight and what genuinely requires a process restart.
- [Settings UI](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/settings-ui/): The in-app Settings page is the schema-driven editor for every per-section TOML file: pools, connectors, dictionary, screens, menus, dashboards, charts and jobs. One builder per concept, a raw Monaco editor as escape hatch, and a Reload button that pushes every change live.
- [Connectors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/connectors/): A connector defines how the framework reaches a data source. Built and edited from Settings → Connectors — three types (SQL, HTTP, API), each with a dedicated builder. Schema is discovered at runtime from the live query; nothing is hand-typed about column types.
- [Audit trail](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/audit-trail/): Recipe — automatically populate created_by, created_at, updated_by, updated_at columns on every write, without trusting the client. The framework's form-layer LOGIN and SYSDATE defaults do the work.
- [Bulk import](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/bulk-import/): Recipe — let operators upload a CSV or Excel file and import its rows into a database table. Validates per row, reports successes and failures, leaves the database untouched on errors.
- [CRUD over an existing table](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/crud-existing-table/): Recipe — take any existing database table and produce a working list / edit / add / delete UI on top of it in five Settings clicks. The fastest path from 'I have a table' to 'users are using it'.
- [Excel export](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/excel-export/): Recipe — every screen ships with an Excel export by default. Customise the column list, add a server-side aggregation export, or schedule a daily Excel sent to email.
- [Expose data to the AI assistant](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/expose-to-ai/): Recipe — decide which connectors the AI assistant can read, restrict writes, write a good tool description so the model picks the right query. The difference between a useful assistant and one that hallucinates.
- [File upload](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/file-upload/): Recipe — let users attach files to a row (contracts, invoices, photos) and serve them back from the same row. Two patterns: store the file in the database, or store a reference and offload to object storage.
- [Multi-step form / workflow](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/multi-step-form/): Recipe — model an approval workflow with status transitions, per-state visibility of fields, role-gated actions and scheduled escalations. The framework's form conditions + custom actions do the work.
- [OIDC sign-in](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/oidc-sso/): Recipe — wire the framework against Authentik, Keycloak, Azure AD or Okta in 10 minutes. Single sign-on, group-to-role mapping, auto-provisioning, break-glass admin.
- [Row-level access](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/row-level-access/): Recipe — give each user access to only their own rows. Salesperson sees only their customers; tenant sees only their data. The :session_user placeholder and a per-query WHERE clause do the work — no app code, no extra middleware.
- [Scheduled report email](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/scheduled-report-email/): Recipe — every weekday at 08:00, run a SQL aggregate, render it as XLSX, email it to a recipient list. The framework's Nomaflow job + http step + Excel export endpoint do the work.
- [Dashboards](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/dashboards/): A dashboard lays out KPIs, charts and tables over connector queries in a responsive grid. Built and edited from Settings → Dashboards with drag-and-drop panels; every panel picks a data source, a visualisation and an optional drill-down.
- [Dictionary](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/dictionary/): The dictionary holds the metadata that turns raw database columns into a readable UI — localised labels, number formats, BOOLEAN / ENUM / LOOKUP rules, form-layer defaults. Edited from Settings → Dictionary; reused everywhere a connector column is rendered.
- [Form conditions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/form-conditions/): Show, hide, require or disable a field based on the live values of the other fields in the same dialog. The Screens builder exposes three condition slots per field — Visible when, Required when, Disabled when — with an expression editor that suggests field names and previews the evaluation.
- [First app walkthrough](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/getting-started/first-app/): Build a working Liberty app end-to-end in under five minutes: declare a database pool, define a SQL connector, expose a screen with a grid + edit modal and wire it into the sidebar menu — all from the Settings UI, all reloaded live.
- [Project layout](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/getting-started/project-layout/): File map of the two repositories — liberty-next (framework binary) and liberty-apps (per-installation configuration). What lives where, what is committed, what is per-installation, and how LIBERTY_APPS_DIR routes the framework to the apps repo.
- [Why Liberty Framework](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/overview/): Liberty Framework is a low-code platform for building internal applications — admin tools, BI dashboards, integration glue, customer portals — without writing a frontend. Define data sources and screens in the Settings UI; the framework renders the grid, the edit dialog, the dashboard, the assistant.
- [Saved grid views](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/saved-views/): Save a data grid's columns, sort, filters and grouping as a named view — your own views follow you across devices, and an admin can publish shared views with one set as the default. Includes the Summary view — server-aggregated parent rows with lazy-loaded child rows — and day-grain filtering on timestamp columns.
- [Step 1 — Set up the CRM project](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/01-setup/): Start the Build-a-CRM tutorial: install the framework, create an empty crm app, prepare the database tables we'll use across the six steps. End state: framework running, admin signed in, three empty tables ready for customers, deals and activities.
- [Step 2 — The Customers screen](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/02-customers/): Build the first screen of the CRM: a SQL connector that reads + writes the customers table, a screen that turns it into a grid + edit dialog, and a menu entry that opens it. Demonstrates the full pool → connector → screen → menu flow.
- [Step 3 — Deals and relationships](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/03-deals/): Add the Deals screen with a foreign-key lookup to Customers, polish the dictionary so status values render as coloured chips, and add an Activities sub-grid inside the Deal dialog. Demonstrates lookups, the dictionary and parent-child relationships.
- [Step 4 — Sales pipeline dashboard](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/04-dashboard/): Layer a dashboard on top of the existing Deals data: four KPIs, a stacked bar chart by stage, a 'recent activities' table, all sharing a period filter and drilling down to the Deals screen. Demonstrates dashboards, charts and the shared filter bar.
- [Step 5 — Roles and SSO](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/05-auth/): Split the CRM into Sales (full edit), Manager (read + dashboard) and Admin roles. Wire OIDC sign-in against a real identity provider. Demonstrates roles, permissions, OIDC and the per-call permission codes generated by the framework.
- [Step 6 — AI assistant and scheduled jobs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/06-ai-and-jobs/): Wire the AI assistant so it can answer natural-language questions over the CRM data, and add a nightly Nomaflow job that flags deals with no activity in 14 days. Demonstrates AI tool generation, permission scoping for the assistant and the Nomaflow job model.
- [What you can build](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/what-you-can-build/): Concrete use cases for the Liberty Framework — internal admin tools, BI dashboards, ERP administration, integration glue, customer portals, ETL orchestration. Each section shows what the framework does for you, what you still write, and how long it takes.
- [Getting Started](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/getting-started/): Liberty Next — connector-driven low-code framework. Configuration drives discovery: define a SQL or API connector in TOML, expose its queries to a screen or a dashboard, and the React UI builds the grid, the form and the filters automatically.
- [Deploy prebuilt apps](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/deploy-prebuilt-apps/): Stand up the NOMANA-IT product apps on a Liberty install — NomaUBL (separate Java service), Nomasx-1 / Nomajde / Nomaflow bundled jobs (delivered as one liberty-apps wheel). The wheel is materialised by install-apps.sh via a throwaway python:3.12-slim container — no host Python or pip needed — then bind-mounted into liberty-next via the docker-compose.apps.yml overlay.
- [Docker](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/docker/): Stand up Liberty Next as a Docker Compose stack — three layouts (light SQLite, full 5-service production, Swarm) + two TLS overlays + an apps overlay, all wired by ./install.sh and the COMPOSE_FILE chain in .env. ./install-apps.sh adds the licensed apps. ./deploy-swarm.sh drives Swarm. ./backup.sh snapshots every named volume + the apps bind mount.
- [Installation — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/overview/): Stand up Liberty Next from the release/ directory — three Docker layouts (light SQLite, full 5-service stack, Docker Swarm), TLS overlays (Let's Encrypt or operator-provided certs), licensed-apps overlay — all driven by ./install.sh, ./install-apps.sh, ./deploy-swarm.sh and ./backup.sh. Plus a pipx alternative for hosts that don't run Docker. Image lives at ghcr.io/fblettner/liberty-next.
- [Bundled visual tools](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/portainer/): How to use the Portainer and pgAdmin instances that ship with the Liberty Full Docker layout — first-run setup, common operator tasks, Docker socket security trade-offs, Swarm specifics.
- [Running in production](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/production/): Production hardening of the Full Docker / Swarm layouts — TLS, password rotation, OIDC, backups, Postgres tuning.
- [Python server](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/python-server/): pipx install of Liberty Next on a Linux / macOS host — one PyPI wheel (frontend bundle baked in), four CLIs on the PATH, plus the licensed-apps wheel injected into the same venv when applicable. Bootstrap with liberty-admin init-db + liberty-admin run-install-jobs. No Docker, no git clone, no npm build.
- [Traefik](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/traefik/): The Traefik reverse proxy is bundled in the Full Docker and Swarm layouts. Two TLS modes ship as additive compose overlays — docker-compose.tls-letsencrypt.yml (ACME TLS-ALPN challenge) and docker-compose.tls-provided.yml (operator-provided certs). Both are wired by install.sh --ssl <mode> with no manual compose edits.
- [Upgrading](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/upgrading/): Upgrade a Liberty install — backup, pull the new image, up -d. Image tag pinning, Swarm rolling updates, rollback.
- [The Monitoring page](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/monitoring/dashboard/): Card-by-card walkthrough of the Monitoring page — KPI strip, Pools, Connected users, Held locks and the live Log tail. What each column means and when to act on it.
- [Health endpoints](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/monitoring/health-endpoints/): The framework's two machine-readable status endpoints — /health for liveness and /info for runtime introspection. Use them in load-balancer probes, container orchestrators and external monitoring.
- [Monitoring — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/monitoring/overview/): Liberty's built-in Monitoring page surfaces what's happening right now — connected users, held row locks, per-pool SQLAlchemy stats, runtime info and the live log tail. Plus the framework's health endpoints for external monitoring.
- [Administration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/administration/): Operating Nomaflow at scale — single-replica vs multi-replica, the scheduler lock, restart behaviour, run history retention, permissions, backup.
- [Bundled jobs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/bundled-jobs/): The Nomaflow job catalogue shipped with the liberty-apps wheel — install / preload / refresh / sync / SOD / audit jobs that drive Nomasx-1 and Nomajde without the operator writing a single line of TOML. Run from Nomaflow → Catalogue → ▶ Run now, schedule via the standard scheduler, or trigger from CI.
- [Change packages](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/change-packages/): Capture every tracked data write into a reviewable package — old → new diffs grouped by entity, exclude entries cherry-pick style, submit / approve / reject the package, export a JSON bundle and apply it on another environment with full pre-image drift detection. The canonical use case is promoting JD Edwards security from dev to prod.
- [Concepts](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/concepts/): The Nomaflow mental model — jobs, runs, steps, schedules, triggers, retry, parameters. Read this once and the rest of the documentation maps cleanly.
- [Custom Python steps](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/custom-python/): Write your own Python callable for a Nomaflow step — function signature, the StepContext object, accessing connectors, logging to the run, handling cancellation, returning structured output.
- [Getting started](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/getting-started/): Build your first scheduled Nomaflow job in ten minutes — open the Jobs page, create a job, add a SQL step, set a cron schedule, watch the first run land in the history.
- [Catalogue](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/jobs/catalog/): The Jobs page — every job listed with its last-run state, next fire and the per-job actions: enable toggle, ▶ Run now, ✕ Cancel, ✎ Edit, Run-with-parameters modal.
- [Create a job](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/jobs/create/): Walk through the Nomaflow Job editor — identity, schedule, parameters, steps, retry, alerts — building a real job from a blank slate, with every field explained.
- [Schedules](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/jobs/schedules/): Cron syntax for Nomaflow, the timezone rule, the Schedule view that previews upcoming fires across every job, and the patterns most installs settle on.
- [Notifications](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/notifications/): Route Nomaflow job events — success, failure, long-run — to Slack, email or generic webhooks. Configure channels once at framework level; jobs pick recipients.
- [What is Nomaflow](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/overview/): Nomaflow is the scheduler and orchestration engine bundled with the Liberty Framework — cron-scheduled jobs, linear step pipelines, retry / backoff, run history with live log tail. No external worker, no broker, no companion daemon.
- [Run history](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/runs/history/): The Runs page and the Run detail drawer — every fire of every job, with per-step timing, inputs / outputs, the live log tail and the abort / replay actions.
- [Troubleshoot](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/runs/troubleshoot/): A run failed, a step hangs, the schedule isn't firing, cancellation doesn't work — checklists and concrete fixes for every common Nomaflow incident.
- [Steps](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/steps/): The five Nomaflow step types — sql_query, sql_copy, python, http, ldap_sync — what each one does, the fields it accepts and when to reach for it.
- [Hourly API pull](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/workflows/api-pull/): Recipe — pull from a third-party REST API every hour, transform the JSON payload in a Python step, write rows into a SQL target with retry and idempotent upsert.
- [Conditional cleanup](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/workflows/conditional-cleanup/): Recipe — a daily cleanup job that runs a destructive purge only when a threshold is crossed, using a SQL Query step for the count and a guarded Python step for the delete.
- [Scheduled database sync](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/workflows/scheduled-sync/): Recipe — a nightly job that streams rows from an operational store into a reporting store with SQL Copy, retry on failure and Slack notification on success.
- [UDC Codes](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/master-data/udc-codes/): User Defined Codes — the individual values inside each UDC type, with inline grid editing for bulk maintenance.
- [UDC Types](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/master-data/udc-types/): User Defined Code Types — the catalogue of UDC groups defined in JD Edwards, with inline edit and create from a single grid.
- [Nomajde — The JD Edwards companion application](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/overview/): Nomajde sits next to JD Edwards EnterpriseOne and turns the day-to-day work — master data, security, reporting, monitoring — into one set of grids with inline edits. SQL and AIS API combined, no fat-client navigation, no manual exports.
- [Environments](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/environments/): Maintain the JD Edwards environment list per user and per role — production, test, development, conference room, with the order in which they appear at sign-on.
- [Role Management](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/role-management/): Maintain JD Edwards users and roles in one place — descriptions, attached roles, environments, and the security workbench import workflow.
- [Role Relationships](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/role-relationships/): Maintain the JD Edwards role-inheritance graph in a single grid — pair source and target roles, set effective and expiration dates, bulk-upload from Excel.
- [Security Workbench](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/security-workbench/): Maintain every JD Edwards security entry — application, action, row, column, processing-option, tab, exit, image — on a single grid with inline edit.
- [User Management](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/user-management/): Add, edit and provision JD Edwards users from a single grid — SQL writes the user master and display preferences, AIS REST provisions the security record and the password.
- [global-settings.md](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/admin/global-settings/)
- [Activity log](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/activity-log/): Database-level activity log — every transaction recorded by user on tables of the connected application.
- [Conflicts — Details](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/details/): Line-by-line backing data for every segregation-of-duties conflict — user, both incompatible activities, the objects and the two source roles.
- [Conflicts — Proven](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/proven/): Segregation-of-duties conflicts confirmed by activity log evidence — the user holds the rights AND has actually exercised them on both sides.
- [Conflicts — Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/roles/): Distinct pairs of roles that produce a segregation-of-duties conflict — the role couples to redesign.
- [Conflicts — Summary](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/summary/): Headline view of segregation-of-duties conflicts — number of users in conflict, broken down by business process and risk.
- [Conflicts — Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/users/): Distinct users in conflict on a connected application — the headline list of accounts to remediate.
- [Menus](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/menus/): Application menu tree, level by level, with the JDE objects each leaf launches and the licence component they belong to.
- [OUT — Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/out/components/): Object Usage Tracking summary by licence component — how many users used each component and when it was last touched.
- [OUT — Details](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/out/details/): Object Usage Tracking detail — every (user, object) pair captured by the source system, with last-used date and version.
- [OUT — Objects](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/out/objects/): Object Usage Tracking grouped by object — which programs of a licence component have ever been invoked.
- [OUT — Users / Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/out/users-roles/): Object Usage Tracking with the user's status, type and link — the per-user view of which licence components they actually consume.
- [Rights — Roles / Menus](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/roles-menus/): Role-level rights joined to the menu tree — what each role grants in terms of navigation, by licence component.
- [Rights — Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/roles/): Object-level rights granted at the role level — the backbone of the security model.
- [Rights — Users / Menus](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/users-menus/): Rights joined to the menu tree — what each user can reach, with the menu path leading to each object.
- [Rights — Users / Roles / OUT](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/users-roles-out/): Effective rights union of the declared rights matrix and the objects users actually invoked, as captured by Object Usage Tracking.
- [Rights — Users / Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/users-roles/): Object-level rights pivoted by (user, role) — what each user can run, both directly and through every role they hold.
- [Rights — Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/users/): Object-level rights granted directly to a user — what each user can run, change, add or delete in the source system.
- [Audit Lookup](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/database/audit-lookup/): Detailed audit lookup — for each audited mutation, the before / after value of every changed column.
- [Audit Trail](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/database/audit-trail/): Header of the database-level audit trail — one row per audited operation, grouped by application, date, schema and table. Each row expands to a field-level BEFORE / AFTER diff parsed on demand from the stored DML statement, plus purge and rebuild-values jobs to manage the history.
- [Oracle](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/database/oracle/): Oracle database properties read from each connected application — product, version, CPU, named-users counts, options and storage.
- [CSI](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/csi/): Customer Support Identifier — list of the Oracle support contracts the connected applications are entitled to.
- [Financial Report](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/financial-report/): Financial impact of the non-compliant rows — additional licence cost and three years of support per application × component.
- [JD Edwards](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/jd-edwards/): JD Edwards licence overview — active users, transactional users, dormant accounts and orphan transactional accounts per JDE application.
- [Oracle](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/oracle/): Per-database list of Oracle licence options with a required / not required indicator — the inventory to compare with the licences actually subscribed.
- [Subscribed Licenses](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/subscribed/): Subscribed licences inventory — quantities of each component covered by each CSI contract, grouped by metric and price list.
- [Usage Report](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/usage-report/): Per-application × per-component compliance — observed user counts versus subscribed quantity, with the compliance delta.
- [Nomasx-1 — The compliance and licence-optimisation platform](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/overview/): Nomasx-1 unifies enterprise security, Object Usage Tracking, Oracle and JD Edwards licence compliance and Segregation of Duties into one platform — source-agnostic, audit-ready, on-premise.
- [JD Edwards Licence Audit](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/reports/audit-licences/): A one-click compliance and optimisation audit for a JD Edwards application — licence inventory, real usage, financial exposure and a remediation plan, rendered as a PDF or Markdown deliverable. Bilingual (French default, English available); the report opens on a headline KPI band and inline charts (active-users donut, components-by-usage bar, financial risk by component).
- [Security & SoD Assessment](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/reports/security-sox/): A one-click security-posture and segregation-of-duties review for a connected application — user lifecycle, privileged access, role and object-security hygiene, SoD conflicts and a remediation plan, rendered as a PDF or Markdown deliverable.
- [Assignments](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/assignments/): Active role assignments — which user holds which role, on which application, with effective and expiration dates.
- [Duplicate users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/duplicate-users/): Users with several accounts pointing to the same person (Address Number / Employee ID), grouped by application.
- [LDAP Settings](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/ldap/settings/): Groups AD departments and drives the per-department Excel export of the Users by applications view.
- [Users by applications](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/ldap/users-by-applications/): Cross-tab of LDAP departments and applications, with each user's source-system account and roles — the source view for the per-department Excel export.
- [Users without AD](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/ldap/users-without-ad/): Users known to a connected application but absent from the corporate LDAP / Active Directory — technical accounts, ghosts, or unsynced identities.
- [LDAP Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/ldap/users/): Raw LDAP / Active Directory user catalog fed into Nomasx-1 — Active Directory attributes side-by-side.
- [Roles matrix](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/roles-matrix/): Distinct role combinations held by users on each connected application, with the number of users behind each combination.
- [Roles not used](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/roles-not-used/): Roles defined in the source system but not assigned to any user — the candidates for cleanup.
- [Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/roles/): Catalog of all roles defined in each connected application — application, role identifier, role name, sequence.
- [Users Audit](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/users-audit/): Per-user audit view — identity, organisation, country and last usage by module — for a deep dive on a single account.
- [Users without roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/users-without-roles/): Active users with no role assignment on a connected application — the orphan accounts to investigate.
- [Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/users/): List of users known to Nomasx-1 across every connected application — identifier, name, account status, creation date, last login, last usage, last update.
- [Applications](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/global/applications/): Registry of every connected application — identifier, type, database, host and credentials Nomasx-1 uses to reach the source system.
- [Custom Queries](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/global/custom-queries/): User-defined SQL fragments overriding the default Nomasx-1 queries on a per-application basis.
- [Prerequisite](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/jde/prerequisite/): Inter-component prerequisites — when buying component X requires having component Y.
- [Reclassification](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/jde/reclassification/): Override of the JDE object → SY mapping when the default classification is wrong or missing.
- [Restrictions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/jde/restrictions/): Mutually-exclusive components — when buying component X excludes the right to use component Y.
- [System Code](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/jde/system-code/): Mapping of every JDE System Code to its functional module and to the licence component it falls under.
- [Oracle Features](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/oracle/features/): Catalog of Oracle database features Nomasx-1 tracks, each linked to a licence component.
- [Oracle Options](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/oracle/options/): Catalog of Oracle database options recognised by Nomasx-1 and the licence component each one falls under.
- [Oracle Versions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/oracle/versions/): Catalog of Oracle database versions recognised by Nomasx-1 and their licence component.
- [Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/pricing/components/): Master catalog of licence components — price list, category, friendly name.
- [Metrics](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/pricing/metrics/): Catalog of licensing metrics — Application User, Named User Plus, Processor, Employee, etc.
- [Pricing](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/pricing/pricing/): Unit list price and support fee per component × metric — the price book the financial report uses to compute the cost of non-compliance.
- [Department](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/security/department/): Standalone catalog of AD department / group pairs — the source of values offered as drop-downs across the LDAP screens.
- [Users properties](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/security/users-properties/): Per-user flags — technical, generic, linked, privileged — that drive licence calculations and audit filtering.
- [SoD — Activities](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/activities/): Named activities within each business process — the atomic units the segregation-of-duties matrix combines.
- [SoD — Matrix](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/matrix/): Pairs of incompatible activities — the SoD matrix that defines which activity combinations trigger which risk.
- [SoD — Objects](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/objects/): Source-system programs attached to each SoD activity — the technical objects whose execution counts as performing the activity.
- [SoD — Process](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/process/): Catalog of business processes that group the activities monitored by the segregation-of-duties matrix.
- [SoD — Risks](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/risks/): Named risks within each business process, with the severity level used to weight the segregation-of-duties findings.
- [CLI reference](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/references/cli/): Every Liberty CLI command — liberty-admin (users, roles, jobs, reload), liberty-connectors (test connectors without the web layer), liberty-crypto (encrypt / decrypt / generate master key), liberty-license (verify / inspect a license JWT). Every flag, every output.
- [REST API reference](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/references/rest-api/): Every REST endpoint the framework exposes — grouped by domain: auth, connectors, screens, dashboards, menus, jobs, ai, admin config, healthcheck. URL, method, required permission, request body and response shape.
- [architecture.md](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/technical/architecture/): Liberty Framework architecture overview — Node.js, PostgreSQL, pgAdmin, Airflow, OIDC, Gitea services orchestrated with Traefik reverse proxy.
- [Docker Installation Guide](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/technical/installation/)
- [Deploying Liberty Framework with Portainer](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/technical/liberty-deployment/)
- [Creating Systemd Services for Docker Compose](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/technical/linux-services/)
- [Enable SSL with Traefik](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/technical/post-ssl/)
- [Deploying Installation Tools with Docker Compose](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/technical/tools-deployment/)

## NomaUBL — e-invoicing

- [AI Capabilities](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/ai-capabilities/): Embedded AI assistant for NomaUBL — answers questions about how the product works using the public documentation, and answers questions about your own data (invoices, lifecycle history, validation errors, e-reporting runs) through a small set of read-only tools. Streams replies, surfaces every tool call, supports French and English.
- [Dashboard](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/dashboard/): The NomaUBL home page — a 12-column widget grid with hero KPI cards (Total / In flight / Rejected — IT / Rejected — Business), pipeline funnel, volume chart, recent activity, stale invoices, top failing rules, per-company breakdown, e-reporting coverage and PA round-trip — all governed by a single date-range filter. Scheduler-health monitoring lives on the dedicated Tech Dashboard since 2026.05.6.
- [E-Directory](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/edirectory/): Look up a French company in the INSEE registry by name, SIREN or SIRET, then check whether each match is reachable on the PPF directory for e-invoice delivery.
- [E-Documents](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/edocuments/): Browse every document captured in the NomaUBL archive — not only those that became invoices — with the archived source spool and the generated UBL side by side, and query the same archive over REST.
- [E-Reporting](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/ereporting/): E-reporting declarations to the Plateforme Agréée — generate French flux 10.1 (B2C invoice detail) and flux 10.3 (B2BINT aggregated) for a chosen company, type and period; track each report's lifecycle, resend on demand, download the submitted XML.
- [Integration Errors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/integration-errors/): Failure-analysis tool over the validation table — by-rule cards ranking the top failing rules, a by-event flat table for row-level investigation, and a detailed view that groups events by invoice. Each rule code is decorated with the human description extracted from the bundled Schematron files. Filter by category (UBL / Integration), severity, document key; the Unmatched only checkbox keeps the original orphan-error view one click away. The detailed view exports every event in scope, even collapsed ones.
- [E-Invoicing](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/invoices/): The day-to-day NomaUBL invoice list — search, filter and inspect every invoice; open a detail view to consult parties, lines, VAT, lifecycle and PDF; edit, copy, resend or e-mail invoices; manually set a status.
- [Notifications](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/notifications/): Portal inbox for status-change alerts emitted by NomaUBL — All / Unread tabs, mark-all-read, per-row dismiss, click-through to the linked invoice. Combined with the navbar bell that polls every 30 s and previews the last six entries, the page is the read-side of the notification system shipped in 2026.05.3.
- [Tech Dashboard](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/tech-dashboard/): Operational health page for the IT team: 14 widgets covering JVM heap, GC, threads and uptime, database ping, build info, filesystem free space and file counts, processing throughput, error trend, retry rate, template processing time, active sessions, live process events (START / END pairs from running jobs, plus inline errors), configuration check, database tables, recent errors, and the background scheduler. One round-trip per refresh, no auth required to render the system block.
- [VAT Declaration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/vat-declaration/): Aggregate every invoice for a period on the standard French CA3 form rows — sales / purchases × domestic / intra-EU / outside-EU × VAT rate × invoice type — with drill-down to the individual invoices behind each figure, and one-click Excel and CA3-formatted PDF exports.
- [API Connectors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/api-connectors/): Define generic REST API connectors used by NomaUBL to talk to a Plateforme Agréée, a source ERP (JD Edwards AIS, SAP, NetSuite, custom) or any HTTP service: connection, authentication, endpoints catalogue, and built-in test runner.
- [Custom Lists](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/custom-lists/): Create operator-defined reference lists (code / FR / EN labels) and assign them to grid columns so dropdowns and filters render automatically. Each list can be edited row by row or synced from an API / SQL connector.
- [JD Edwards](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/database-connectors/jdedwards/): Configure the access to the JD Edwards database NomaUBL reads from when extracting BIP outputs: JDBC URL, credentials, schema, BIP table names and post-extraction record handling.
- [NomaUBL Database](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/database-connectors/nomaubl/): Configure the connection to the NomaUBL application database (Oracle or PostgreSQL): JDBC URL, credentials, schema, the full table catalogue (invoice, e-reporting, auth, notifications), the Columns mapping editor, a Validate Schema panel that compares the bundled DDL to the live schema, and a one-click Initialize action.
- [FTP Connectors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/ftp-connectors/): Configure SFTP access to the JD Edwards Enterprise Server so NomaUBL can pull spool files directly from the JDE PrintQueue.
- [List Views](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/list-views/): Edit the per-view column spec (labels, format, alignment, width, filter allow-list) for every NomaUBL list page — Invoices, Integration Errors, Processing Log, E-Reporting — and add new columns from the view's column catalog without writing code.
- [Reference Lists](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/reference-lists/): Catalogue of the standard French e-invoicing reference lists embedded in NomaUBL: ISO/UN/CEN code lists, Factur-X / EN 16931 business term values, and PA-side action and rejection codes.
- [Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/security/roles/): Manage NomaUBL roles: row-based grants stored in F564254 across four tabs — Access (pages + dashboard cards + features), Actions (per-action whitelist), Data scope (companies + row filters), Members. Card list with copy / delete, friendly page labels from the sidebar i18n, granular per-button action grants and column-based row filters that gate the list views, the per-row endpoints and the rendered PDF stream.
- [Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/security/users/): Manage NomaUBL user accounts: create, edit, deactivate or delete users, assign them a role and reset their password.
- [SQL Connectors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/sql-connectors/): Define generic SQL connectors used by NomaUBL to read or write rows on any reachable database — Oracle or PostgreSQL — through named parameterised queries. Each query carries a name, label, description, parameter spec, the SQL itself with :param placeholders, and a Writable flag. The editor has Connection / Queries / Test tabs and the runtime binds parameters through PreparedStatement so values are never string-substituted into SQL.
- [Auto-Retry](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/auto-retry/): Settings → Auto-Retry schedules a daily sweep that replays every invoice in a chosen technical-error status (default 9904 at 3 a.m.) back to the Plateforme Agréée. Multi-status picker, optional lookback window, per-row throttle, shared with the Send Failed card on the Tech Dashboard. The overnight pickup for batches stuck on the PA side.
- [Daily Digest](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/daily-digest/): Settings → Daily Digest schedules a recurring email of the day's integration errors, with the full event list attached as an Excel file. Multiple digests can be configured per recipient subset, each with its own send time, lookback window, severity filter and per-column routing — different teams receive different cuts of the same data.
- [Document Types](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/document-types/): Configure the seven NomaUBL document type codes that anchor the French e-invoicing / e-reporting reform: per-type description, default selection, send-to-PA policy, output mode and file-retention flags.
- [E-Directory](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/edirectory/): Configure the connection to the French PPF (Portail Public de Facturation) directory and the INSEE company search used to validate addressing codes and look up customer information before sending an e-invoice. Two-tab layout: Directory (Enable Check + INSEE Search) and Connector (api-connector picker + per-task endpoint overrides).
- [E-Invoicing](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/einvoicing/): Configure how NomaUBL talks to a Plateforme Agréée (PA) — through a reusable api-connector reference, an optional SFTP fallback for outbound submission, and a status-retrieval section. Four-tab layout: UBL Validation · PA Connection · FTP/SFTP · Status. The api-connector holds the auth flow and endpoints; this page only references it by name and overrides per-task endpoint names when needed.
- [E-Reporting](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/ereporting/): Configure how NomaUBL produces and submits e-Reporting bundles — Sender / Issuer identity, schedule and flux, the api-connector that holds the PA's HTTP transport, and the SFTP fallback for outbound submission. Four-tab layout: Identity · Reporting · PA Connection · FTP/SFTP. paMode = API / FTP / empty replaces the legacy sendToPA Y/N flag.
- [Fetch Invoices](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/fetch-invoices/): Configure which JD Edwards BI Publisher (BIP) jobs NomaUBL retrieves for batch processing, and which document template to use for each.
- [Global](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/global/): Application-wide NomaUBL settings: directories, processing helpers (XSL, Ghostscript), SMTP, AI assistant, license & authentication, and the batch / polling scheduler.
- [OIDC](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/oidc/): Configure single sign-on for NomaUBL: OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE flow, IdP issuer / client / scopes, claim mapping keyed by email, allowed email domains, Google Workspace hd claim enforcement, auto-provisioning with a default role. Drives the login screen jointly with the Auth Mode field on the Global template.
- [Statuses](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/statuses/): Define the invoice lifecycle statuses NomaUBL recognises: regulatory code, internal Tag, bilingual labels, the event name expected by the Plateforme Agréée, the Collect flag for PA polling, and the Groups that drive the dashboard counters and SQL filters. Search box, expandable per-status form, multi-select groups with coloured chips.
- [Extract Archive](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/extract/extract-archive/): Extract an archived invoice document from the NomaUBL database back to disk — original source XML (F564230) or generated UBL 2.1 (F564231) — by document key (FEDOC / FEDCT / FEKCO).
- [Extract BIP](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/extract/extract-bip/): Extract a BIP (BI Publisher) job's payload from the JD Edwards Print Queue — input XML (F95630) or rendered output (F95631) or both — to a directory on the NomaUBL server.
- [Extract FTP](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/extract/extract-ftp/): Browse a remote SFTP server and download a file to a local directory on the NomaUBL server — uses the SFTP credentials configured in FTP Connectors.
- [NomaUBL — The unified e-invoicing platform](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/getting-started/): NomaUBL bridges any ERP to the French e-invoicing reform — UBL generation, pre-submission validation, Plateforme-Agréée routing, lifecycle tracking and operations on a single platform. Source-agnostic, PA-agnostic, ready for the 2026 RFE.
- [Configure](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/configure/): After the install, every connector, scheduler interval and operational setting is configured from the Settings UI — not by hand-editing config files. Start the service, sign in, then walk through the Configuration section.
- [Install and layout](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/install-and-layout/): Run -install (directly via java -jar, or via the nomaubl.sh / nomaubl.cmd wrapper) to provision an environment. Understand the directory layout produced — config / input / process / ubl / template / shared resources — and how to install several environments side by side on Linux, macOS or Windows.
- [Installation — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/overview/): Stand up a NomaUBL server — JDK 17 + an Oracle or PostgreSQL database + the JAR. Runs as a long-lived Java process, one per environment, started through the nomaubl.sh wrapper. Optional systemd unit and reverse proxy for production.
- [Requirements](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/requirements/): What the host needs before installing NomaUBL — JDK 17, an Oracle or PostgreSQL database, OS support matrix, ports, file-system permissions and the optional reverse-proxy / TLS layer.
- [Service supervision](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/service-and-systemd/): Run NomaUBL as a long-lived service on Linux/macOS or Windows — nomaubl.sh or nomaubl.cmd for start/stop/status, a systemd unit (Linux) or NSSM Windows service (Windows) for auto-restart on boot, and an optional nginx reverse proxy in front for TLS and a friendly hostname.
- [Upgrade](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/upgrade/): Move an installed NomaUBL environment forward to a new release. One command — nomaubl.sh upgrade on Linux/macOS or nomaubl.cmd upgrade on Windows — handles the JAR swap, schema migrations, reference-data merge, customer XSL merge and service restart. Writes a full report and keeps a rollback backup.
- [Action Bindings](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/actions/): Bind the regulatory seller actions surfaced in the invoice detail modal — Payment Received, Credit Note, Corrected Invoice, Send Completed, Cancel Accounting, New Invoice, Resend to PA — to one or more API or SQL connector calls. Per-binding multi-call list with Stop on failure flag, response chaining via {call.N.fieldName}, and a Scope selector that lets each company override the default e-invoicing template.
- [Command Line](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/command-line/): NomaUBL command-line interface — service control via nomaubl.sh, direct modes of the JAR (install, serve, xml, ubl, fetch-import, fetch-status, fetch-single, fetch-all, extract) with every argument and flag explained.
- [Documents](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/documents/): Configure how each document type is parsed from a source XML spool, read from a UBL invoice, or pulled live from a SQL query / REST API, then transformed for processing and rendered as PDF.
- [File Versions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/file-versions/): Browse the NomaUBL environment file tree, view and restore previous versions, edit text files in-app, view PDFs, and export / import multi-file packages between environments.
- [Notification Rules](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/notification-rules/): Define which invoice status changes generate a notification, what they say, who receives them and through which channels (portal inbox, email, external API call). Each rule is a notification-rule resource saved in config-notifications.json; a synchronous Test panel lets you fire a rule end-to-end before flipping it on for production.
- [PDF Templates](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/pdf-templates/): First-class library of reusable PDF layouts. Each template is a pdf-template resource referenced by document templates by name. Edit once, propagate everywhere via a full-screen visual builder — palette of sections on the left, live preview in the centre, inspector with options + custom-block tree editor on the right.
- [Processing Log](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/processing-log/): Browse the NomaUBL runtime log — every START / END / intermediate event recorded during XML, UBL, BIP and FTP processing. Group events by job to see status and duration at a glance, or switch to the flat event stream for forensic analysis.
- [Monitoring — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/monitoring/overview/): Where to look when running NomaUBL in production — the in-app Tech Dashboard, the Processing Log, the service log file, the build-info / license endpoints. Plus the patterns to wire external monitoring.
- [Service and logs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/monitoring/service-and-logs/): Operate NomaUBL from the host — wrapper status (nomaubl.sh on Linux/macOS, nomaubl.cmd on Windows), the log file for live diagnostics, /api/build-info and /api/license for machine-readable checks. Patterns for external alerting and log forwarding.
- [Process Document](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/processing/document/): Single processing entry point for one or many invoice files. The pipeline is selected automatically by the document template's source property — XML spool (XSL → UBL) or already-formed UBL 2.1 — so the same form covers both flows.
- [Extract and Process](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/processing/extract-and-process/): Chain an extraction (Archive / FTP / BIP) and a processing run (XML or UBL) in a single click — equivalent to running an Extract page then the matching Processing page back-to-back.
- [Process API](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/processing/process-api/): Execute an API connector endpoint defined in Configuration → API Connectors — pick a connector and an endpoint, override parameters at runtime, inspect the HTTP response and any extracted value.
- [Database Tables](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/database-tables/): NomaUBL database schema reference — every table that backs the application: invoice archive, UBL header / lines / VAT, lifecycle events, validation errors, processing log, e-reporting, notifications and authentication. Functional descriptions, primary keys and field references for Oracle and PostgreSQL.
- [Reason Codes](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/reason-codes/): Reason codes attached to invoice life-cycle statuses for the French e-invoicing reform — refusal (B2B), PA rejection and irregularity codes from XP Z12-012 Annex A.
- [Status Reference](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/status-reference/): Invoice life-cycle statuses for the French e-invoicing reform — codes 200 to 501 (XP Z12-012) with actor, phase, mandatory/factoring tags and allowed actions.
- [UBL Reference](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/ubl-reference/): UBL field reference for the French e-invoicing reform — every BT field with its XPath, cardinality and example, grouped by section (header, supplier, customer, tax, totals, line, etc.).
- [Release Notes](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/release-notes/): NomaUBL release notes — every user-visible change shipped in the platform, version by version, in reverse chronological order. Mirrors the in-app Release Notes page.
- [Fetch Input](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/fetch-input/): Batch-automated equivalent of Extract and Process — scan a directory or the BIP Print Queue, pick items in a checkbox list, and run the same Extract → Process pipeline on every selected item.
- [Import](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/import/): Confirm that invoices submitted to the Plateforme Agréée have actually been imported — async import polling that updates each pending 9906 invoice to 10 (Deposited) or 9907 (PA rejected the import).
- [Retrieve Statuses](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/retrieve-statuses/): Pull lifecycle status events from the Plateforme Agréée — XP Z12-012 codes 200, 201, 206, 207, 210, 213… — and apply them to the local lifecycle table and the invoice header. Watermark-based incremental retrieval.
- [Allowances / Charges](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/allowances-charges/): UBL Defaults — Allowances / Charges tab. Sets the fallback reason text and reason code per direction (BR-42 for allowances, BR-43 for charges); the ChargeIndicator picks the pair at emit time.
- [Business Process Type](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/business-process-type/): UBL Defaults — Business Process Type tab. French Cadre de facturation (BT-23) — invoice nature (goods / services / mixed) and lifecycle stage (deposit / already paid / final / subcontracting / multi-vendor / e-reporting).
- [Country & Classification](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/country-classification/): UBL Defaults — Country & Classification tab. Sets the source-side format for the line country of origin (BT-159) and the fallback classification code, scheme listID and version (BT-158).
- [Currency Code Mapping](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/currency-code-mapping/): UBL Defaults — Currency tab. Default currency (BT-5) and source → ISO 4217 currency code mapping.
- [Document Type (BAR Routing)](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/document-type-bar-routing/): UBL Defaults — Document Type tab. BAR routing classification (B2B / B2G / B2BINT / B2C / OUTOFSCOPE / ARCHIVEONLY / DOCUMENT) used to dispatch the document inside the Plateforme Agréée.
- [French Legal Notes](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/french-legal-notes/): UBL Defaults — Notes tab. Document-level legal notes (BT-22) carrying mandatory French wording — payment delay, recovery fee, general terms — with note-type prefix.
- [Invoice Type](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/invoice-type/): UBL Defaults — Invoice Type tab. Default UBL invoice type code (BT-3) and rule-based selection driven by source XML conditions.
- [Overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/overview/): How NomaUBL's UBL Defaults work — a base defaults file (ubl-defaults.xsl) plus optional per-template override layers, resolved field group by field group at generation time.
- [Payment Code Mapping](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/payment-code-mapping/): UBL Defaults — Payment tab. Default payment means code (BT-81) and source → UBL code mapping based on UNCL 4461.
- [Scheme IDs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/scheme-ids/): UBL Defaults — Scheme IDs tab. ISO 6523 / UNTDID 1153 / EAS scheme identifiers attached to SIREN, SIRET, GLN, electronic endpoint and delivery location.
- [Suppliers / Companies](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/suppliers-companies/): UBL Defaults — Suppliers tab. Directory of seller (AccountingSupplierParty) records used as defaults when the source XML omits them, keyed by company code.
- [UBL Header Defaults](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/ubl-header-defaults/): UBL Defaults — Header tab. UBL version, customization ID (BT-24), default country (BT-40 / BT-55) and per-template date input format.
- [Unit of Measure Mapping](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/unit-of-measure-mapping/): UBL Defaults — Units tab. Default unit code (BT-130) and source → UN/ECE Recommendation 20 unit code mapping.
- [VAT Categories](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/vat-categories/): UBL Defaults — VAT tab. Default VAT category, zero rate, source → UBL category mapping (BT-118 / BT-151) and category → VATEX exemption-code mapping (BT-121).
- [Validate](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/validate/): Validate a UBL document against XSD schema and Schematron business rules — straight UBL or upstream XML transformed to UBL via a template's XSL pipeline.
- [XML Viewer](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/xml-viewer/): Open any XML file — local or server-side — in a Monaco editor with syntax highlighting, pretty-print, line numbers and save-to-server. The lightweight companion to the validator and the XSL Editor.
- [XSL Editor](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/xsl-editor/): Map source XML spool fields to UBL 2.1 business terms (BT codes) through a visual form — no hand-written XSLT required. AI-assisted auto-mapping included.

## JDE API reference

- [NOMABC - Barcode 128 for BI Publisher](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/bip-api/nomabc/): Simple java class to encode string and display barcode 128 with BI Publisher RTF template
- [NOMABIP - Java package with Oracle BI Publisher API](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/bip-api/nomabip/): API to integrate easily JDEdwards and BI Publisher regardless of JDEdwards Tools Release
- [Open source API for JD Edwards and BI Publisher](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/getting-started/): Open source API for JD Edwards and BI Publisher
- [JDEBIP - Export XML source or PDF Output from JD Edwards BLOB fields](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/jde-api/jdebip/): This class can be used to export blob column for BI Publisher from JD Edwards Database. This class can be extended to export BLOB for all tables
- [JDEBSN - Export source code for BSFN from JD Edwards BLOB field (F98780R)](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/jde-api/jdebsfn/): This class can be used to export blob column for BSFN from JD Edwards Database. This class can be extended to export BLOB for all tables
